title: request-multiplex-ttl-fidelity-curve
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Produce multi-dimensional latency vs perceptual-quality curves for combinations of request multiplexing (shared execution slots), microbatch sizes, and prefix cache TTL strategies. Unlike prior sweeps that focused on token-level metrics, this study ties model-config perturbations to human-aligned quality signals (automatic QA-based scoring + semantic similarity) and concrete rollout thresholds to decide safe config changes for Hosted and Dedicated tiers.

Scope: sweep across 3 models (open-7b, open-13b, redwood-small-1), 4 multiplexing levels (0, 2, 4, 8 concurrency per worker), 5 microbatch sizes (1, 2, 4, 8, 16), and 3 TTL strategies (aggressive: 30s, default: 300s, conservative: 3600s). Measure latency (p50/p95), tail variance, tokens/sec, and quality using: automatic answer-EM/F1 for the eval set, embedding cosine retention for context fidelity, and a learned QA-critic score calibrated against 200 human annotations.

Why different: previous tickets enumerated batching/KV cache sensitivity primarily via raw token-level regressions. This ticket ties config deltas to a combined "perceptual quality" metric with explicit rollout decision rules (quantified acceptable delta for P50/P95 vs quality) so that Console can automatically suggest config deltas with safety margins.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end harness that runs sweep permutations and outputs a single CSV with all metrics (latency p50/p95, throughput, EM, F1, embed-cosine, QA-critic) per permutation.
Dashboard with interactive contour plots for latency vs QA-critic where users can filter by model and region and export selected configs.
Decision rule implementation: a small config change is considered safe to auto-suggest if QA-critic delta >= -0.8 and p95 latency change <= 10% and p50 <= 5%.
Regression alerting rule defined and wired to quality-monitoring: any config change in staging that produces QA-critic drop >1.2 triggers rollback and a P0 incident runbook.
Results validated against 200 held-out human judgments with at least 90% agreement on directionality of quality regression detection.
plan: Week 1: Implement harness modules for multiplexing parameterization and TTL simulation; add metric collectors for QA-critic and embed-cosine.
Week 2: Run full factorial sweep on a small fleet (staging cluster); generate initial contour plots and identify obvious tradeoff modes.
Week 3: Expand to dedicated capacity profiles and run on representative workload traces; gather human annotation batch (200 items) for calibration.
Week 4: Ship dashboard, alerting rules, and PR with auto-suggest policy; prepare rollout playbook and follow-up tickets for automation of A/B rollout.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Harness skeleton checked in (GH: PR#8723) with mock multiplexing knobs. Basic p50/p95 collectors added.
2026-03-05: Embedded QA-critic model integrated as a lightweight microservice behind /eval/critic endpoint; initial calibration run shows sensible ordering across microbatch sizes.

2026-03-09: First full sweep (all combos) completed on small staging run; found several configs where microbatch=8 + TTL=30s produced 12% p95 improvement but QA-critic -0.9 on open-13b (needs human review).
2026-03-12: Human annotation batch kicked off (200 examples). Dashboard prototype uploaded to internal Grafana (link in attachments).
decisions: Use QA-critic (learned ranker calibrated to human labels) as primary perceptual-quality proxy instead of only EM/F1 to capture instruction-following degradation.
Treat multiplexing level as independent knob from microbatch size for this study (though future work will study joint adaptive controllers).
Default 'safe' thresholds chosen conservatively: QA-critic delta -0.8 and p95 <= 10% to favor availability; thresholds to be revisited after human validation.
blockers: Annotation vendor backlog delaying labels (expected 48-72 hour delay).
Staging GPU quota temporarily reduced; need ENG-infra approval for extra nodes to run full sweep at scale.
